title: What's the ultimatum game?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a discussion of lottery winnings and sharing money, then explain the ultimatum game, devised by game theorist Ariel Rubinstein in the early 1980s. They cover German economists' experiments showing people often offer far more than rational maximization predicts and reject lowball offers, the dictator game variant, and a capuchin monkey fairness study at Emory University. They discuss nonverbal cues, altruism, and karma. Closing segment previews a how stuff works article on what would happen if a roller coaster safety harness broke, ahead of Chuck's trip to Cedar Point.

segments.title: Opening sponsor reads
segments.summary: Sponsor reads for a camera and Visa fraud protection before the show begins.

segments.title: Lottery winnings and sharing
segments.summary: Hosts discuss who they would share lottery winnings with, and a Melbourne man who shared a 13 million dollar win with the friend who suggested he buy the ticket.

segments.title: Explaining the ultimatum game
segments.summary: Josh introduces Ariel Rubinstein's ultimatum game from the early 1980s, explaining a proposer splitting twenty dollars and a responder who can reject the offer, and the rational maximization prediction.

segments.title: German experiments test the ultimatum game
segments.summary: German economists tested the game in real life. Average offers were about 37 percent, and about half of low offers were rejected, contrary to Rubinstein's prediction.

segments.title: Dictator game variant
segments.summary: The dictator game removes the responder's veto. Around 76 percent of players still split the money evenly, which the hosts find puzzling.

segments.title: Chimps and capuchin monkey fairness
segments.summary: Chimps showed no sense of fairness, while capuchin monkeys at Emory University reacted angrily when given grapes instead of cucumbers for the same task.

segments.title: Nonverbal cues, altruism and karma
segments.summary: Hosts discuss whether players read nonverbal cues, observer effects, and whether altruism and karma explain generosity.

segments.title: Roller coaster preview and sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck mentions his upcoming Cedar Point trip and the Millennium Coaster, and Josh previews the article on a broken roller coaster safety harness. Closing sponsor read follows.
